sections.text: You went for open play against 3...h6 with 4.d4 and kept the initiative, helped by 14...Bh3?, a Black blunder. You found 15.Rxe5+! and kept winning ground with 16.Qf3 and 17.Qxb7, then 18.Rxe7 put you at +5.6.

Black gave it back with 21...Rcf8, but 22.Ba3 missed 22.Rxf7 and 23.Re3 missed 23.Rxg7+, which carried a fork and a skewer. With each missed chance the position went from winning to lost, and then back again: 25.Kxh2!, 26.Kh1! and 27.Rxf3! were precise defensive moves that put you at +3.9.
Even at +7.1 after 27...Rxf3 you still had a win, but low on time you played 28.Rg1. The engine's 28.Qa8+ was a back rank check that kept everything under control. Instead 28...Rh3# ended it.

review.headline: A reckless 4.Nxe5 that your opponent could not punish, followed by a tactical win

sections.text: You opened with a normal Two Knights Italian, then grabbed on e5 with 4.Nxe5. That was a real mistake: after 4...Nxe5 you were a piece for a pawn down (-3.2) and the engine wanted 4.Ng5 instead.
Credit to you for how well you used the next chances. Black replied 5...Bc5, and 6.d4! was the right shot. It forked the bishop on c5 and the knight on e5, which Black could not handle.

8.Qd5 created another fork on c5 and e5 and also pressured b7 and d7. Black's 8...Nxb3 was a blunder, and you took the best route with 9.Qxe5+. That check also hit g7 with the rook on h8 behind it, so Black had to trade queens with 9...Qe7 10.Qxe7+ Kxe7 and recapture with 11.axb3.

From there it was simple: you developed with 12.O-O and 13.Nc3, picked up pawns with 15.Nxc7 and 16.Nxa8, and finished with a steady rook and bishop attack. Black ran out of time at move 30 while you were far ahead.

review.turning_point: 8...Nxb3 was the decisive error from Black. You found 9.Qxe5+ and the evaluation jumped to +4.6.
review.focus: Look at 4.Nxe5: before capturing in the opening, ask what recaptures. 4.Ng5 was the safer way to keep the initiative.
